recipes.name: Pot Roast, Vegetables, and Beer
ingredients_raw: 1.5 pounds potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
1 (12 fluid ounce) can or bottle dark beer
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Heat olive oil in a Dutch oven. Brown pot roast on all sides in hot oil; remove from pan and set aside.

Stir onion and garlic into hot oil and cook until onions are just softened and golden brown, about 5 minutes. Add carrots, mushrooms, and potatoes to the pot; cook and stir until they begin to color, 2 to 3 minutes. Mix flour into vegetables; stir continuously for 1 minute. Add beef stock and beer; bring to a boil, stirring continuously. Stir in bay leaf, thyme, brown sugar, mustard, tomato paste, salt, and pepper; place pot roast back in the pot and cover with a lid.
Bake in the preheated oven until beef and vegetables are completely tender, about 2 1/2 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Pot Roast, Vegetables, and Beer
raw_recipe.description: A beef pot roast is braised in dark beer with vegetables, garlic, mustard, and thyme until fall-apart tender. Easy to prep yet packed with flavor!

review.reviewBody: Want to influence relatives and win friends? This recipe was excellent! However, I used what I had available. Coors Lite beer, chicken stock w/ one beef bullion cube and a course mustard with horseradish. Wow! This was good. Potato's and carrots were perfect and I did not cook them as long on top of the stove as suggested prior to putting the roast into the oven. First meal made with my new Tromintina brand 6.5qt Dutch Oven -red (WALMART Web ordered $54.00 Nice!).

Fabulous recipe. I re-hydrated a dry "gourmet" mushroom mix (from Costco), using about 1 1/2 cups mushrooms and 2 cups very hot water. Also used unpeeled fingerling potatoes. Covered for about one hour. The brine was beautiful, dark, and aromatic, and I added that to the pot along with the mushrooms. I baked it in a cast iron enamel crock pot in the oven at 350F for about 4 hours. The flavor was amazing, and the meat was so tender, you didn't even need a knife. This is a keeper. Not sure why someone would say it tasted like beer. I used dark beer, and it just added a great wholesome flavor to the whole dish. Frankly, I think it's better than using red wine.

This was fantastic, and it will be made again and again. I did make some adjustments based on what I had and other suggestions. I left out the potatoes and made mashed potatoes to serve with instead. I also seasoned the meat with salt and pepper before browning. I used two beef bouillon cubes in water, substituted some garlic chile mustard that needed used, used about 1 tsp of ground thyme, added the flour after I added the liquid (that one was a total oops), and used a porter for my beer. Cooked as directed, then removed the meat and vegetables and cooked down the liquid into a lovely sauce on the stove which I poured over the mashed potatoes, meat, and veggies. OHMIGOD this was good.

This came out great, but I modified it. I didn't have dark beer,(I only like Belgium White), so I used two cups of Merlot Wine instead.

Also, I made a roux with the flour, 2tbs flour and 2tbs butter. 

It was a hit!

This was great! Time constraints had me, brown meat and then put in crock pot. I didn't have dark beer, but the results were still moist and yummy. I'm looking forward to eating the leftovers.
31 May 2012 Still don't own a dutch oven, but I did buy porter for the recipe. Worked great in the crockpot after searing the roast in a fry pan. Still fabulous.
After reading comments I tweaked it. Added horseradish and chunks of fresh tomato in addition to tomato paste. Extra garlic. Seasoned the meat before searing with a spicy steak rub. So good.

I have made many pot roasts recipes but the hubby really liked this one.I used my slow cooker on low for 8 hrs. I followed the recipe exactly except I didn't precook the carrots or potatotes and used the only beer I had which was Kokonee . I put everything cooked into the crock pot stirred in the potatoes and carrots and placed the pot roast on top. It came out perfectly. We don't eat gravey but if i had wanted some I would have have to add more flour as the juices were not thickened.Thanks for the recipe.

My first try at a pot roast and it came out very well. I used a slow cooker rather than a dutch oven in the oven but it was fine. My wife loved it. For the dark beer I used a very nice Mendocino stout which made the sauce somewhat bitter, so I had to adjust it with a bit of brown sugar. I suggest that others use a milder dark beer.

So. Darn. Good. I made a few minor adjustments, but kept it mostly the same. I omitted the flour just because I prefer it that way and used Squirt soda instead of beer (that's what I had, but it made it so tender good). I also added a little celery salt and rosemary. I baked it in my dutch oven for 5.5 hours at 250 and added the veggies for the last hour so they weren't all mushy. When the veggies became tender, I pulled out the meat and gravy, turned my oven to broil, put the dutch oven with veggies back into the oven with the top off and took them out when they were golden-brown. Gorgeous. Husband and I have decided that we're going to be making a lot more meals in our dutch oven and will definitely be doing this one again (and again and again).

This was amazing! I used water and a Bouillion cube and seasoned the meat before adding it to olive oil. I also kept the garlic cloves whole and just smashed them to release the flavors, but have the whole cooked cloves at the end. I also used a table spoon of ground time instead bc I don't care for the stemmy texture and i didn't want it to be so pungent. It was delish and perfect to warm up my family on a snowy, winter night.
Nice flavors, but I think it is better without the sugar. I also would recommen that you saute the paste with the vegs, adds to the complexity of the flavor profile.

Excellent one pot meal. I'll certainly make it again. I followed the recipe almost exactly but I forgot to get the beer so I used 12 oz of Cabernet I happen to have. Also, I added a half pound of celery chunks.
Only change needed was dried thyme as I didn’t have fresh. Great gravy!
Warning! Don't use a beer with added nitrogen. It ruins it. Bitter, bitter, bitter. I used a Guiness Stout. Ruined two pounds of beef and a whole lot of effort!
This recipe is easy & delicious. I didn’t have dark beer so I used red wine as another reviewer suggested & it was great…that was the only change I made. .
very rich and satisfying!

This recipe is a winner when made with red wine instead of beer. I used baby red potatoes cut in half w/ skins on. While labor intensive at the beginning, just popping it in the oven for 2.5 hours was definitely a plus! I will add this to my rotation for Sunday dinners.
Really good pot roast; nice and tender. The potatoes were a little bland-- I would have kept the skins on for better flavor.

This Pot Roast is very flavorful and easy to make. I have made it with dark beer and also with red wine, both were very good and added their own flavor notes. This last time I made it, I didn't have any beer or wine and didn't want to go to the store in the storm. I added balsamic vinegar which gave it a different and very good flavor.

This is a fantastic base recipe for you to take and adapt to your tastes. I do recommend doing a rub on the meat before browning it; but just make how it sounds good to you. I used a local porter as the dark beer, and I have no complaints, other than I need a bigger pot.
